title: Lifecycle phases
task_statement: Run an AI system through ordered lifecycle phases with gates, and plan model retirement and migration. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Lifecycle phase gates
components.first_principle: Each phase closes only when its artifact exists, so later work cannot replace earlier work. (Inference)
steps: Close discovery when each requirement has a metric, a threshold, and an owner. (Inference)
Close design when options are priced and decision records exist. (Inference)
Close handoff when runbooks, alert owners, and a tested rollback path exist. (Inference)
Close monitoring when triggers fire and a review follows. (Inference)
Return to the earliest skipped phase when a later phase fails. (Inference)
pros: A failed later phase points to the gate that the team skipped. (Inference)
Gates limit how much a fix costs after each later phase. (Inference)
cons: Gates can slow a small team that has no handoff. (Inference)
Emergencies skip gates, so the record must catch up later. (Inference)
use_when: The system has real users, money, or compliance scope. (Inference)
Several teams hand off operation of the system. (Inference)
do_not_use_when: A reversible demo has no real data. (Inference)
A live outage needs an immediate fix before any record exists. Write the record after the fix. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Name the alert owner before the handoff gate closes. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Test the rollback path before live traffic. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Name the signer for each gate. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Record an emergency path that writes the record after the fix. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Scale the gate review to the team size. (Inference)
Compare the cost of a gate with the cost of a later fix. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D6.5. Expect a live failure where a phase was skipped. The credited answer returns to the skipped phase, not to more monitoring. (Inference)
components.trap: More dashboards look like progress, but they measure a design that has no requirements. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: When a later phase fails, return to the earliest skipped gate. (Inference)
components.exam_tip: A higher error rate with no thresholds points to discovery, not to monitoring tools. (Inference)

components.name: Model lifecycle states and retirement
components.first_principle: A model has one of four states, active, legacy, deprecated, or retired, and requests to a retired model fail.

nodes.label: Usage export by API key and model

steps: Check the model status on the deprecations page in each release cycle. (Inference)
Export usage from the Usage page to find deprecated models.
Read the downloaded file to find each API key and model in use.
Test the replacement model well before the retirement date. (Inference)
Move all traffic to the replacement before the retirement date.
pros: Retirement dates appear on the deprecations page ahead of time.
The usage export shows which API keys still call deprecated models.
cons: Deprecated models are likely to be less reliable than active models.
Some retirement dates are tentative, so the deadline can move.
use_when: An application calls a model with a deprecated or legacy status.
A team plans a model change before a known retirement date.
do_not_use_when: The application calls an active model and no change is planned. (Inference)
A decision must use a model that the platform has already retired. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Export usage by model and API key before each retirement date.
constraints.combination: Test the replacement before the date. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Use the replacement that the deprecations page names.
Notify the owner at the first deprecation notice. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Check each platform, because Amazon Bedrock and Google managed platforms set their own retirement schedules.

constraints.choice: Compare the replacement with cost per completed task before cutover. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D6.5. Expect a deprecation notice with a near retirement date. The credited answer migrates before the date, to the named replacement. (Inference)
components.trap: A model switch made only at the retirement date causes an outage, because requests to a retired model fail.
components.decision_rule: Migrate to the named replacement before the retirement date, and test the replacement first.
components.exam_tip: A deprecated model still serves requests, but its retirement date sets the deadline.

components.name: Workspaces per environment
components.first_principle: Every request runs in exactly one workspace, so each environment needs its own workspace for keys, usage, and limits.
steps: Create one workspace each for development, staging, and production.
Scope each API key to the workspace that it serves.
Set rate limits for each workspace, based on its environment.
Set a spend limit on each workspace that is not the Default Workspace.
Promote the tested model ID from staging to production. (Inference)
pros: Each environment has its own keys, usage, and limits.
Usage reports separate the environments by workspace.
cons: Each extra workspace adds administration work. (Inference)
The Default Workspace cannot be renamed, archived, or deleted.
use_when: Development and production need different rate limits.
do_not_use_when: A single prototype has one user and no production traffic. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Scope each API key to one workspace.
constraints.combination: Use a key that is not workspace-scoped with a workspace header for calls across workspaces.

constraints.choice: Set development rate limits lower than production rate limits.
Set a spend limit on each workspace that is not the Default Workspace.
constraints.combination: Keep production traffic out of the Default Workspace, which has no spend limit. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Give each team access only to its own workspace.
constraints.combination: On Google Cloud, give each team its own project, because roles apply to every workspace in a project.

constraints.choice: On Claude Platform on AWS, create each workspace in the AWS region where the data must stay.

native_services.text: Each workspace binds to one AWS region, and IAM policies grant or deny access per workspace.

components.exam_tie: D6.5. Expect a question on separate environments. The credited answer separates development, staging, and production into workspaces with their own limits. (Inference)
components.trap: One shared workspace with a label convention looks simple, but keys and limits then mix across environments. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Create one workspace for each environment that needs its own limits or reports.
components.exam_tip: The Default Workspace cannot have spend limits, so production needs its own workspace.

flowchart LR

  M --> I[Iteration]
  I --> D
  R[Retirement notice] --> X[Export usage]
  X --> P[Replacement tested]
